audits.title: WTP8.08 Snapshot audit of adherence to hospital infection prevention and control policy pertaining to the monitoring of IV cannulae. A quality improvement project
audits.standard: Trust infection prevention and control policy: cannulae correctly dressed and labelled, documented in the electronic record and assessed twice daily
audits.setting: Hospital-wide inpatients, small district general hospital (STDH)

cycle1.result: 38% of inpatients (n=86) had a cannula; just over 30% documented in notes; only 10 had a date label; 26 had spoiled dressings; 18 had thrombophlebitis. Time since insertion 24 to 240 hours.

audits.intervention: Results presented at grand round and a poster of recommendations created (second cycle planned).
audits.citation: Dawson E, Jatania J, Walls M, Fish T, Wharrier J. WTP8.08 Snapshot audit of adherence to hospital infection prevention and control policy pertaining to the monitoring of IV cannulae. A quality improvement project. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_13). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf166.402.

audits.title: Clinical audit documenting insertion date of peripheral intravenous cannulae.
audits.standard: RCN and local guidelines: document insertion date of peripheral cannula; change uncomplicated cannula at 72 hours
audits.setting: Surgical wards, district general hospital (Dewsbury and District General Hospital / Eastbourne DGH guidelines)

cycle1.result: 13.8% of cannulae had been in place for more than 72 hours; poor documentation compliance despite staff awareness of guidelines.

audits.other_findings: Most staff nurses knew the 72-hour standard; poor compliance was linked with increased superficial phlebitis.
audits.citation: Biswas J. Clinical audit documenting insertion date of peripheral intravenous cannulae. Br J Nurs. 2007;16(5):281-283. doi:10.12968/bjon.2007.16.5.22998. PMID: 17505373.

audits.title: Failure of a poster-based educational programme to improve compliance with peripheral venous catheter care in a tertiary hospital. A clinical audit.
audits.standard: In-house infection control recommendation to record date and time of PVC insertion
audits.setting: Adult inpatients, Royal Darwin Hospital, tertiary hospital

cycle1.result: Any dating of PVC insertion recorded in 13.4%.

cycle2.result: Any dating recorded in 16.1% (P = 0.27, not significant).

audits.other_findings: 1109 inpatients across both phases; patients with bacteraemia risk factors more likely to have date recorded (P = 0.03).
audits.citation: Morse L, McDonald M. Failure of a poster-based educational programme to improve compliance with peripheral venous catheter care in a tertiary hospital. A clinical audit. J Hosp Infect. 2009;72(3):221-226. doi:10.1016/j.jhin.2009.03.009. PMID: 19464755.

audits.title: Accuracy in documentation of peripheral venous catheters in paediatric care: an intervention study in electronic patient records.
audits.standard: Complete and accurate recording of peripheral venous catheters in the electronic patient record
audits.setting: Wards of a large paediatric university hospital

cycle1.result: Recording of any kind in 85-93%; 1 of 22 observed complications documented.

audits.intervention: Structured standardised template for recording peripheral venous catheters in the electronic record.

cycle2.result: Significant increase in complete recording; side and size recording improved; none of the complications (n = 17 and n = 9) documented.

audits.other_findings: Overall recording of insertion did not improve; EPR still not accurate after intervention.
audits.citation: Förberg U, Johansson E, Ygge BM, Wallin L, Ehrenberg A. Accuracy in documentation of peripheral venous catheters in paediatric care: an intervention study in electronic patient records. J Clin Nurs. 2012;21(9-10):1339-1344. doi:10.1111/j.1365-2702.2011.03949.x. PMID: 22243530.

audits.title: Implementation of a paediatric peripheral intravenous catheter care bundle: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.standard: SUCCESS PIVCS insertion and maintenance care bundle
audits.setting: Tertiary paediatric hospital, Lady Cilento Children's Hospital, Brisbane

cycle1.result: PIVC failure 50 (49%); first-attempt insertion success 45%; junior doctor first-attempt escalation 72%.

audits.intervention: Mnemonic care bundle (SUCCESS PIVCS) implemented via visual aids, workshops and change champions.

cycle2.result: First-attempt insertion success 62% (risk ratio 1.37); junior doctor first-attempt escalation 41%.

audits.citation: Kleidon TM, Cattanach P, Mihala G, Ullman AJ. Implementation of a paediatric peripheral intravenous catheter care bundle: A quality improvement initiative. J Paediatr Child Health. 2019;55(10):1214-1223. doi:10.1111/jpc.14384. PMID: 30702181.

audits.standard: IV line insertion and maintenance checklist; aim to reduce infiltration and phlebitis by 50% over 2 months
audits.setting: Paediatric emergency room, PGIMER Chandigarh (tertiary care)
audits.intervention: IV line insertion and maintenance bundle over PDSA cycles: sterile mobile trays, audit and feedback, organisational change, infection control nurse and QI team

audits.title: Improving Vascular Access Dressing Integrity in the Acute Care Setting: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.standard: Target of 80% of dressings with all 4 corners intact without reinforcement at day 7
audits.setting: Two intermediate care units in 2 hospitals, Methodist Hospitals, Indiana

cycle1.result: Existing dressing with education did not achieve the 80% goal.

audits.intervention: Sequential 2-week trials of updated and new dressings with education, then addition of a liquid gum mastic adhesive

cycle2.result: Dressings with added gum mastic adhesive exceeded the 80% goal; no exposed insertion sites and no MARSI in any protocol.

audits.other_findings: Post-project data on 30,049 vascular access sites showed the same effect; it became standard of care.
audits.citation: DeVries M, Sarbenoff J, Scott N, Wickert M, Hayes LM. Improving Vascular Access Dressing Integrity in the Acute Care Setting: A Quality Improvement Project. J Wound Ostomy Continence Nurs. 2021;48(5):383-388. doi:10.1097/won.0000000000000787. PMID: 34198309.

audits.title: Evaluating peripheral intravascular catheter insertion, maintenance and removal practices in small hospitals using a standardized audit tool.
audits.standard: Standardised PIVC audit tool for insertion, maintenance and removal practices

cycle1.result: 22.6% did not report a visual infusion phlebitis score at least daily; 48% did not document daily dressing assessment.

audits.other_findings: 57.6% inserted on wards; removal reasons: no longer required 63%, phlebitis 4.8%; no bloodstream infections.

audits.title: The Appropriate Use and Care of Peripheral Intravenous Cannulas: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.standard: Local PIVC care bundle criteria; target adherence 90-100% for each criterion

cycle1.result: Adherence scores for all criteria lower than in cycle 2 (figures not reported in abstract).

audits.intervention: Interventions for improvement (details not reported in abstract).

cycle2.result: Site of insertion and acceptable site 100% (fully adherent); indication 90-100%; 24-hourly assessment and bundle completion 75-90% (partial); date of insertion <75% (non-adherent).

audits.other_findings: No cannula-related complications; date of insertion remained non-adherent.
audits.citation: Aung SL, Sengupta A, Win NN, Rajkanna J, Oyibo SO. The Appropriate Use and Care of Peripheral Intravenous Cannulas: A Quality Improvement Project. Cureus. 2025;17(1):e76954. doi:10.7759/cureus.76954. PMID: 39758858.

audits.title: Improving Documentation of Intravenous Cannulation in a Resource-Limited Teaching Hospital: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Audit.
audits.standard: IV cannula documentation standards (source not named in abstract)

cycle1.result: Compliance ranged 0 to 68%; insertion site 4%; aseptic technique 2%; complications 4%; flushes/patency checks 0%.

audits.intervention: Standardised IV cannula documentation sticker with staff training, posters and ward reminders.

cycle2.result: Most parameters ≥ 95%; insertion site 100%; aseptic technique 96%; complications 96%; flushes/patency 80%.

audits.other_findings: Flushes and patency checks remained lower than other domains.

audits.title: Enhancing IV Cannulation Documentation in a Resource-Limited Setting: A Quality Improvement Project From Dongola Specialized Hospital.
audits.standard: International standards for IV cannulation documentation (patient identifiers, insertion details, aseptic technique, site monitoring, removal data)
audits.setting: Internal Medicine Department, Dongola Specialized Hospital

cycle1.result: Most parameters documented in 2% or fewer records (e.g. cannula gauge 2%, indication 2%, aseptic technique 2%, inserter's name 2%).

audits.intervention: Structured IV cannula documentation sticker and brief educational sessions.

cycle2.result: Cannula gauge 100%; indication 96%; aseptic technique 86%; inserter's name 92%.

audits.other_findings: Improvement was seen across all fields.

audits.title: An audit of peripheral catheter care in a teaching hospital.
audits.standard: Correct attachment and dressing of peripheral venous catheters (no named guideline or target)
audits.setting: General medical and surgical wards, Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Birmingham (teaching hospital)

cycle1.result: 68 PVCs incorrectly attached, 49 (71%) of these with inflammation vs 5/32 (16%) correctly attached (P < 0.01).

audits.other_findings: Inflammation was also associated with catheters in situ over 48 h.

audits.title: A quality improvement project: Reducing bloodstream infection by improving adherence to the care bundle of peripheral vascular catheters at the COVID-19 treatment centre.
audits.setting: COVID-19 treatment centre, Sungai Buloh Hospital
audits.intervention: Three PDSA cycles; the third focused on leadership by senior clinicians to enforce the bundle and ANTT, and ultrasound guidance for difficult insertion.

cycle2.result: BSI rate fell from 6.41 to 4.34 per 100 admissions after the third cycle.

audits.other_findings: The first two PDSA cycles did not improve BSI rates; non-compliance with aseptic non-touch technique was identified.
audits.citation: Tan KT, Benedict SLH, Gani YM, Chidambaran SK. A quality improvement project: Reducing bloodstream infection by improving adherence to the care bundle of peripheral vascular catheters at the COVID-19 treatment centre. Med J Malaysia. 2022;77(5):590-596. PMID: 36169071.

audits.title: Care for peripheral intravenous catheter: an audit in two French university hospitals.
audits.standard: French Society of Hospital Hygiene recommendations for PIVC care
audits.setting: Seven wards in two university hospitals, Hospices Civils de Lyon

cycle1.result: Patient identity checked in 50%; hand hygiene 82.5% before insertion, 54% before infusion and 13% before removal; flushing in 82.5% of insertions and 66% post-infusion; gloves at insertion 47%.

audits.other_findings: Occlusion was the commonest reason for removal (14.3%).

audits.title: Reducing bloodstream infections with a peripheral intravenous catheter bundle at 38 Australian hospitals: A quality improvement initiative.
audits.standard: ACSQHC Management of Peripheral Intravenous Catheters Clinical Care Standard (2021)

cycle1.result: Insertion attempts documented 32%; overall documentation 74%; ultrasound for difficult insertion 21%; consumer education and consent documented 47%.

audits.intervention: PIVC bundle: service-wide policy, nursing documentation, I-DECIDED tool, audit tool, risk reporting, prefilled saline flush syringes and updated consumer information.

cycle2.result: Insertion attempts documented 65%; overall documentation 83%; ultrasound 30%; education and consent 80%; overall SABSI down 21% and local PIVC infection down 55%.

audits.other_findings: Prefilled syringes saved 49 s per use; staff satisfaction above 90%.
audits.citation: Isles N, Ray-Barruel G. Reducing bloodstream infections with a peripheral intravenous catheter bundle at 38 Australian hospitals: A quality improvement initiative. Infect Dis Health. 2026;31(2):100400. doi:10.1016/j.idh.2025.12.001. PMID: 41719943.

audits.title: Nurse-led peer audits as a driver for improved peripheral intravenous catheter care and reduced bloodstream infections.
audits.setting: Adult internal medicine, surgical and geriatric wards, General Hospital Sint Lucas, Ghent, acute secondary care hospital

cycle1.result: Insertion site visibility 12.7%; PLABSI 0.81 per 10,000 patient-days in 2022.

audits.intervention: Weekly bedside audits moving to a nurse-led peer audit model with a digital questionnaire and real-time dashboard feedback.

cycle2.result: Insertion site visibility >90%; PLABSI 0.29 per 10,000 patient-days in 2025.

audits.other_findings: 6718 audits in total (June 2022 to December 2025); documentation- and time-dependent processes improved less.
audits.citation: Bogaert C, De Greve A, Verfaillie C. Nurse-led peer audits as a driver for improved peripheral intravenous catheter care and reduced bloodstream infections. J Hosp Infect. 2026;173:211-218. doi:10.1016/j.jhin.2026.04.013. PMID: 42092463.

audits.title: Peripheral intravenous catheters: the road to quality improvement and safer patient care.
audits.standard: Peripheral venous catheter care bundle based on Health Protection Scotland drafts (insertion and maintenance measures, duration less than 72 h)
audits.setting: Infectious Diseases Unit, Ninewells Hospital, Dundee
audits.intervention: Monthly PDSA cycles with daily review of PVC necessity, weekly audit and feedback displayed on the ward, monthly patient safety meetings, new PVC dressings and new PVC care plans

cycle2.result: Compliance improved by 1.11% per week to 82% (95% CI 0.6-1.6%; P=0.0001).

audits.other_findings: Further roll-out of the bundle across the hospital was needed to improve compliance.
audits.citation: Boyd S, Aggarwal I, Davey P, Logan M, Nathwani D. Peripheral intravenous catheters: the road to quality improvement and safer patient care. J Hosp Infect. 2011;77(1):37-41. doi:10.1016/j.jhin.2010.09.011. PMID: 21130520.
